en: Taal Volcano emits sulfur dioxide, which is a colorless gas with a pungent odor.
Seawater in the Puerto Princesa Underground River is a homogeneous mixture of liquid water and dissolved salts.
The tamarind tree produces fruits containing tartaric acid, which gives liquid sinigang its sour chemical property.
Lava erupting from Mayon Volcano cools into solid basalt rock through a physical change of state.
Fibers from the Musa textilis species possess high tensile strength, making them excellent solid materials for ropes.
The limestone caves of Sagada form when slightly acidic groundwater chemically dissolves solid calcium carbonate rock.
Jose Rizal used the chemical properties of lemon juice to write invisible ink letters that darken when heated.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol are solid limestone mounds shaped by the physical weathering of liquid rain.
The giant Tridacna clam secretes solid calcium carbonate minerals to continuously build its hard protective shell.
Jeepney engines combust a mixture of liquid diesel fuel and oxygen gas to generate kinetic energy.
The solid steel suspension cables of the San Juanico Bridge possess high tensile strength to support heavy loads.
Water vapor condensing on the cold glass windows of a Manila MRT train undergoes a physical state change.
